photos.c: The start of the London-Brighton Relay 1932. Carter (B1) finished 4th on the first stage with 21-22, breaking the previous course record. One place ahead was Birchfield's R.R. Sutherland (C1).
Sydney Wooderson congratulates Carter after the latter's inter-club win at Wimbledon, 1940.
Tom Carter, who was our fifth scoring man.
1941 Twenty years later Harry walks to the start of the Surrey County Cross Country Championships with Tom Carter who won the title.

This picture was taken during the 1931 - 34 period and shows some famous Belgravians of that time. We have no record of the race concerned except to know that J.E.FLOWER (right) was the winner.

W.L.(Wally) BAYLISS, our then General Honorary Secretary, is the timekeeper, while W.H.(Harry) HARE, Past President and Honorary Treasurer, acts as recorder. The man gaining a sneak preview of the result is the ubiquitous TOM CARTER, and the man with the eyeful, A. (Micky) WALKER.
Charlie Smart leads the 3 miles field in the Southern Counties A.A.A. Championships of 1939 at Motspur Park. Tom Carter (No. 32) lies 4th with Ted Stimpson (No. 25) 9th.
L to R   A.Allum, H.E.Footer, A.E.Taylor, A.R.Shaw, S.Warboys Arthur Penny, J.E.Flower, H.W.Shields, Tom Carter and W.A.Rice

John Morris, Fred Denny, Richard Dorman, JOE COLEMAN, John Llewellin,Ed. Crossingham, Tom Carter, Ted Stimpson, Kneeling; Graham Seatter, Ron Day, John Hall.
"MR. PRESIDENT 1989" DIGS IN. Leo Coy puts the final touches to planting of the Belgrave Harriers Centenary Tree watched by Carl and Barbara Lawton, Harry Porter, Chas Manning and Tom Carter.
Has he just fixed the lock again, been on the roof to check the guttering - or has he simply called in to keep an eye on the place before setting off to Battersea for a home meeting?

Below: Twenty four year old Tom Carter (B1) gets a good start in the London to Brighton Relay of 1932. He placed fourth on that first stage, inside the previous course record and setting the team up nicely for a set of bronze medals.
Above: Always full of enthusiasm, Tom, Club Captain in the '30s and '40s, celebrates the Guardian Gold Cup win in 1992 with Track & Field Captain of the '90s - Lenny Paul.

As a way for the Club to say thank you to Jack Goswell for all his hard work in fund raising over the years, first running the football competition and then the "200 Club", Tom organised a little ceremony at Belgrave Hall where Jack was presented with a carriage clock by our 1993/94 President. Left to right: Trevor Williams, John Davies (hidden), Dave Davies, Alan Mead, the late Tom Carter and Jack Goswell
